ES asks extension surface on assessed path. fetch_url is a fixed built-in tool with no constraint on arguments ("not independently constrained") → W? Tool args not constrained, and MCP manifest trusted. I'd say W (arguments not independently constrained). Actually fetch_url schema is just a string; destination not constrained → W.

CVSS: AV — attacker is a fetched web page; agent is a CLI, needs the user to ask it to fetch a page → UI=A (user must take specific action), AV=L? Entry via content the user asks to fetch → attack vector local (relies on user acting, opening content). AV:L (relying on user to open content is L per FIRST: "relies on a user on that system to act (such as opening a file or visiting content)"). But the page is on a mock web server—still requires local user interaction. AV=L. AC=L. AT=N. PR=N (attacker is web page author, no privileges on agent). UI=A. VC=H? Reads .env credential file — confidentiality high (specific high-value credential disclosure). VC=H. VI=N? The agent doesn't modify anything on this path... just reads and fetches. VI=N, VA=N. SC/SI/SA: subsequent systems — attacker's host is the receiver; the .env credentials belong to user's workspace... The disclosure is of the vulnerable system's data to the attacker—no subsequent system impact beyond that. SC=N? Subsequent system: the .env file / workspace — it's part of the same? Data store is a subsequent system? CVSS: exfiltration of data from data store via agent → SI? Workspace .env is a separate data store; its confidentiality affected → SC=H? Hmm. The .env file contents are disclosed — the file store could be considered subsequent system. Commonly scored: agent reads secret and sends out; the secret's system (user's machine) is same host. I'll set SC=H, SI=N, SA=N with rationale that the workspace data store is a subsequent system. Or keep everything within vulnerable system VC=H and SC=N. Since agent process is the vulnerable system and .env file lives in the workspace (not inside agent process), it's a subsequent system. But it's the same local machine... CVSS doesn't care about machine. I'll do VC=H (secret reaches model context and goes out?) Actually the "vulnerable system" is the agent process including its tools; the .env file is outside. SC=H seems right. Simpler: VC=H (secret loaded into agent context and echoed to attacker) — I'll score VC=H, SC=N, SI=N, SA=N? The attacker host is not impacted adversely. Fine.

Actually the primary impact: credential file disclosure → confidentiality. I'll put VC=H, SC=N, SI=N, SA=N, VI=N, VA=N.

Automatable: no human beyond the trigger? Requires user to ask agent to fetch the page → No (needs user interaction). "Yes/No" — attack requires the user's request; partial. Say No.
